To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Web Service approach to Grid middleware is a good choice, that it works, that the community is ready to adopt it and that the new ARC is already available for production use.
ARC is a well-proven Grid middleware solution that is now being re-engineered to meet the requirements for a modern, standards-compliant Grid solution.

(i) the ARC community has successfully introduced the Web Service technology to the core ARC middleware, and (ii) the new WS-based ARC components are ready to replace the old ones in production environments, which will be done gradually over the coming years, and will lead to the next generation of ARC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of a new generation of Grid middleware based on Web Services technologies.
development and implementation of new components and services for ARC, as well as their integration into the production middleware and deployment at large-scale infrastructural sites.
the development of a modular and interoperable Grid middleware, which is able to provide a seamless and secure access to distributed resources for a large variety of scientific applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ARC is on its way to becoming a full-fledged Grid middleware, and is ready to be used in production environments.
the new ARC is not a middleware any more, but a service-oriented platform for building distributed computing solutions.
the new ARC is a true Web Service based Grid middleware, and that it is a key element of the EGI middleware ecosystem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to successfully implement a number of WS based interfaces into our middleware and to make them available for the community.
we have been able to introduce the WS technology in a well-accepted way into the ARC middleware, and that the new services are already used in production by the NDGF.
the new ARC middleware is not only more modular, but also more flexible and more portable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the WS approach is not only a way to improve interoperability, but also a way of introducing new features into a mature Grid middleware.
modularity is a must in the design of a modern Grid middleware, and interoperability is the only way for such a middleware to be widely adopted.
the Web Service approach, when properly designed, is a powerful tool to achieve true cross-system interoperability.
